pr_title: Add support for stating accepts/consumes metadata is required or not
pr_body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a pull request to our repo. -->

<!-- Once all that is done, you're ready to go. Open the PR with the content below. -->

**PR Title**
Add support for stating accepts/consumes metadata is required or not

**PR Description**
This PR uses  ```AcceptsMetata``` for extensions method rather ```ConsumesAttribute```

Fixes #35849

review_comments: I think this and the other from-body coverage we lost can be re-added with tests using TestEndpointRouteBuilder.
Aren't those covered with the metadata tests in ```EndpointMetadataApiDescriptionProviderTest.cs``` ? What will TestEndpointRouteBuilder test ?

I assume you mean DelegateEndpointRouteBuilderExtensionsTest? That should continue testing that the correct `IAcceptsMetadata` gets added.

We still need to test that the `IAcceptsMetadata` gets used and properly turned into the proper `SupportedRequestFormats` and `ParameterDescriptions`.

See the following test ```MapPost_BuildsEndpointWithCorrectEndpointMetadata``` in ```DelegateEndpointRouteBuilderExtensionsTest```.  It's exactly checking that we have the correct metadata. I can add an assertion to check if the type isRequired.  Anything else ? or Can you point me to an additional test class ?
That doesn't test anything about the `ApiDescription` that gets generated though.
I'll admit this I'm asking for more of an integration test, but we should have those and they already exist in this test class.
I added some more end to end tests.

Super unnecessary, but you can do this:

```suggestion
            additionalContentTypes.CopyTo(allContentTypes.AsSpan(1));
```
Any perf impact ?
I'm guessing the for loop is probably faster, but this lets you save trees if you're like me and print out all PRs to review.
Is there a test that verifies this is `true` if `IsOptional` is not configured?

Lets discuss this later. I have a concern with the ```isOptional``` for ```ConsumesAttribute``` when you don't use a type. The following case might have some unintended behaviors because of the inferred binding: 

 ```C#
    app.MapPost("/todo", [Consumes("application/custom0", "application/custom1")] (Todo todo) => {...})
```
so when type is null, we assume the type information comes from the body parameter, and therefore we can use the optionality from there?
@davidfowl That's correct. Any unintended consequence that this change can cause that you may know of ?.

@davidfowl @halter73 and @pranavkm , I think this test is not needed anymore since we are adding the default content type (```application/json```) as ```IAcceptsMetadata``` when we call the ```RequestDelegate``` Create method. Any thoughts ?
Why isn't this required? Shouldn't we test it anyways?
This is fine, understood.
This is an interesting side effect of this change. The type isn't required right?

Oh yes, an interesting one when you use ConsumesAttribute without a type. Accepts requires a type, so we are good on that one.  while testing with Swashbuckle, I noticed that it  won't take null values for some of the description properties (Type, Model, etc.). So passing a void type is away to mitigate that. Also, the user  can look at the open api result and quickly realize that what they declared is not correct. so, I am now convinced this is more helpful to the user.

Let's also add a test case for the super-weird scenario where an implicit from-body parameter is overridden. I think we have this already for attributes with the AddsRequestFormatFromMetadata() test, but not for the extension method.
@davidfowl FYI, I removed this test as well since we are now skipping creating the api parameter description from body and only getting the value from the metadata. I, also adjusted some other tests.

Can we reimplement this test by calling `MapPost` on the `TestEndpointRouteBuilder` and verify the optionality still flows correctly from the `RequestDelegateFactory` to the `EndpointMetadataApiDescriptionProvider` via `IAcceptsMetadta`?

I suspect
yes added tests.
